title: A/B Testing LLM Features — GrowthBook, Statsig, and the Vibes Problem

questions.question: Which expression is the treatment effect used by z_statistic?
options: The pooled success count divided by n_total
questions.explanation: z_statistic returns (p_b - p_a) / se, so a positive result means the observed B rate exceeds A.

questions.question: Which fixed-sample assumptions are hard-coded in the demo for the default calculation?
questions.explanation: fixed_sample_size has alpha=0.05 and power=0.80 defaults, represented by z_alpha=1.96 and z_beta=0.84.

questions.question: When is the sequential boundary first eligible to stop the simulation?
options: Only after both n_a and n_b exceed 100
After the first request in either group
As soon as p_a equals p_b
questions.explanation: The loop checks that both n_a and n_b exceed 100 before calculating z and the always-valid threshold.

questions.question: How does the sequential threshold grow with the accumulated sample?
options: It equals the observed lift percentage
questions.explanation: simulate computes the illustrative always-valid boundary from 2*log(1/0.05) plus log(n_total), then takes the square root.

questions.question: Why does main multiply the traditional sample size by 1.4 for the LLM-adjusted value?
options: To remove all Type-I error control
To force every test to stop at 100 observations
questions.explanation: The demo applies adjusted = int(required * 1.4), explicitly labeling the factor a buffer for non-deterministic model outcomes.

questions.question: What do n_a and n_b mean when simulate stops sequentially?
options: The number of variants in the catalog
The pooled count before random assignment
The observations accumulated up to the stop point
questions.explanation: The returned counts are incremented inside the loop and can be below max_n when the z-boundary fires, especially for the strong-signal case.
